audit.why: FAV / 7.5-difficulty and the chart Skill / Mel / Skill / Nautilus x4 match the mirror audit (mel__nautilus) exactly and the 60% win rate over 15 games. No chart flip needed.
audit.corrected: Left as-is; mirror agrees row for row.

audit.why: Spikes are level 2-3 (full pattern), Mel's level 1-2 poke window, level 6 Depth Charge, first item. Confirmed against both kits; only the wording of the level 6 and first-item spikes needed the reflect fix.
audit.corrected: Spike levels kept; text corrected to name Rebuttal and its 38s rank-1 cooldown.

audit.whatIsWrong: Text repeatedly says Mel's R reflects your damage. It does not. Golden Eclipse (R) is a global Overwhelm-stack strike with no reflect; the projectile reflect is Rebuttal (W), 250 range, 38/35/33/29/26s cooldown.
audit.why: Dredge Line (Q) and Depth Charge (R) are both flagged projectile, so Rebuttal is the one ability that can turn your own engage back on you — the decisive interaction of the matchup, and it was attributed to the wrong slot.
audit.corrected: Rebuttal (W) reflects Dredge Line and Depth Charge; bait it before hooking. It is down 38s at rank 1. Golden Eclipse instead detonates Overwhelm stacks globally, so chip damage kills you after you walk away.

audit.whatIsWrong: No mention of Searing Brilliance's execute threshold or that Rebuttal creates terrain that can cut a no-dash Nautilus off.
audit.why: _missing lists execute-threshold, autoreset-burst-tell and terrain-cuts-retreat for this pairing.
audit.corrected: Golden Eclipse / Overwhelm execute added to the late text; Rebuttal named as the wall you hold Flash for.

edits.before: Level 1 is genuinely even — you have no W or E yet, so just soak her Q poke at CS range and don't flame yourself for it; she actually edges level 2 because her ranged Q chunks you while you have no way to close the gap. The whole plan is reaching level 3: once Q + W + E are up you flip the lane. Bait her R — it reflects your damage, so don't dump your combo into it — then Q-pull her, let your passive root tick, and E-slow so she cannot walk out of your W splash-burn.
edits.after: Level 1 is genuinely even — you have no W or E yet, so just soak Radiant Volley at CS range and don't flame yourself for it; she edges level 2 because that 950-range Q chunks you while you have no way to close. The whole plan is reaching level 3: once Dredge Line, Titan's Wrath and Riptide are up you flip the lane. Bait Rebuttal (W) — it reflects Dredge Line straight back — then hook her, let Staggering Blow root, and Riptide so she cannot leave the splash-burn.

edits.before: Depth Charge homes in and knocks her up from range — her R reflect and W/E zoning never get to fire before she's locked.
edits.after: Depth Charge homes in and knocks her up from range — Rebuttal is the only answer that reflects it, and it is down 38s at rank 1.

edits.before: Depth Charge is an undodgeable homing lock — it knocks her up from range so her R reflect and W/E zoning never get to fire.
edits.after: Depth Charge is an undodgeable homing lock, but Rebuttal (W) reflects it — check that her 38s shield is spent before you press R.

edits.before: Bait her R reflect window, then Q-pull her into passive root and E-slow so she eats the full splash-burn trade
edits.after: Bait Rebuttal's reflect window, then Dredge Line into Staggering Blow and Riptide so she eats the whole splash-burn

edits.before: Catch your engage on her R reflect so your own combo damage bounces back
edits.after: Catch your hook on Rebuttal (W) so Dredge Line reflects and your engage dies there

edits.before: You hold this lane even into items because Mel has no dash and no hard disengage — your Q-R chain still catches her, and one full lock is enough to delete a squishy mage. Unlike a hypercarry she doesn't outscale you into a window where she kites you forever; she just becomes a poke threat you have to flank. Keep buying engage tankiness, ward her flanks, and look to R her in teamfights the moment she shows for a poke — she's the same un-escapable target she was at level 3.
edits.after: You hold this lane even into items because Mel has no dash and no hard disengage — your Q-R chain still catches her, and one full lock deletes a squishy mage. She does gain reach: Golden Eclipse strikes every Overwhelm-stacked enemy from anywhere on the map, so walking away on low HP is not safe. Keep buying engage tankiness, ward her flanks, and R her the moment she steps up to poke — she is the same un-escapable target she was at level 3.

notes: Mel's reflect is Rebuttal (W), not her ultimate — the old text had it on R in four places. Golden Eclipse is a global Overwhelm detonation with an execute feel; that is now stated in late. Mirror (mel__nautilus) already sets the chart to Skill/Mel/Skill/Nautilus x4, which matches this side, so no level-chart pair proposed.
